# Caddy (HTTPS) — root-context

App at /, Caddy terminates TLS on https://localhost:9443/ with the repo's certificate and forwards over plain HTTP to the backend. No X-Forwarded-Proto rule is needed: reverse_proxy derives it from the connection. An explicit certificate and a host-less site address keep automatic HTTPS from requesting a certificate or starting a redirect listener. Served over HTTP/2; HTTP/3 is switched off in the shared Caddyfile.

Proxy URL on `https://localhost:9443`: `/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

Caddy site block (`caddy/https/root-context/vaadin.caddyfile`), mounted as
`/etc/caddy/vaadin.caddyfile`:

```caddyfile
# App at /, Caddy terminates TLS on https://localhost:9443/ and forwards over
# plain HTTP to the backend.
#
# There is no X-Forwarded-Proto rule: reverse_proxy derives that header from the
# connection's TLS state on its own, as Traefik does. Compare
# `RequestHeader set X-Forwarded-Proto "https"` (Apache) and
# `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme` (NGINX).
#
# Caddy's automatic HTTPS stays out of the way without being switched off. The
# certificate is given explicitly, so nothing is requested from an ACME CA, and
# the site address names a port but no host, so no HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect
# listener is started on :80 either.
#
# The site serves HTTP/2 through ALPN, like the Traefik and HAProxy siblings
# and unlike NGINX's `listen 443 ssl`. HTTP/3 is switched off in the shared
# Caddyfile. When reproducing an upgrade by hand, give curl --http1.1: over h2
# the Connection and Upgrade headers are forbidden and silently dropped.
:443 {
	tls /etc/caddy/tls/localhost.crt /etc/caddy/tls/localhost.key
	import common
	reverse_proxy vaadin:8080
}
```

The global options and the `common` snippet this file imports (the
access log and the compression allowlist) come from the shared
[Caddyfile](../../Caddyfile), mounted read-only over the image's own
`/etc/caddy/Caddyfile`. It imports this file, so the two only load as a pair.
